encoding: Lossless WebP. Alpha and every visible RGBA pixel are unchanged; invisible RGB where alpha is zero is normalized by the encoder. Original generated PNGs are retained in the authoring workspace.

sheets.prompt:
Create a single SQUARE transparent PNG sprite atlas for a polished Chinese children's English-learning website. Exactly TWO equal-width COLUMNS and FOUR equal-height ROWS: EIGHT separate horizontal 2:1 illustration cells in reading order, top-left to bottom-right. Absolutely no visible grid lines, borders, panels, labels, letters or text. Each illustration is a compact isolated 3D cartoon vignette with soft rounded shapes, gentle warm lighting, pastel lavender/cream/sky-blue accents and clean transparent surroundings. Keep generous transparent breathing room inside each cell and do not let objects cross cell boundaries. Within each 2:1 cell, cluster the artwork toward the RIGHT two-thirds, leaving the LEFT side mostly transparent, so website text can sit separately to its left. All objects must remain completely inside their cell. This is subtle decorative artwork, not a worksheet or UI screenshot. Match the friendly high-quality 3D cartoon look and the boy/girl faces in the supplied homepage reference; when a human is needed use those same brown-haired characters, blue hoodie boy or pink hoodie girl, without graduation hats. People only where specified; otherwise use objects. Transparent background throughout, no scene walls or photographic backdrop. Each cell must communicate its own category distinctly. Cell 1: Greetings and polite expressions: the reference boy in his blue hoodie smiles and waves one anatomically correct hand, with a tiny friendly gift/flower beside him.
Cell 2: Numbers and quantity: a charming wooden abacus, three pastel counting blocks and a few golden counters. No printed numerals or letters.
Cell 3: Colors: a rainbow of paint pots, colored pencils and a rounded artist palette, vivid but soft.
Cell 4: Shapes and size: a circle, triangle, square, ruler and small-versus-large toy blocks.
Cell 5: Time and clocks: a friendly round analog clock, wristwatch and little hourglass, pale lavender and blue.
Cell 6: Weekdays and dates: a desk calendar with empty grid squares and a tiny appointment pin, no writing.
Cell 7: Months and seasons: a miniature tree showing spring blossoms, summer leaves, autumn leaves and winter snow, a calm circular arrangement.
Cell 8: Weather and climate: soft sunshine emerging from a cloud, a few raindrops, umbrella and snowflake.
